brief.title: Driver dispatch & proof-of-delivery platform
business_goals: We need the system to auto-assign the nearest available rider to each order.
We had a spike in "item not received" disputes last quarter and it cost us badly on chargebacks.
Last month we had a rider go completely off-route for two hours and nobody noticed until the customer called to complain, that shouldn't be able to happen again.
We also need this to integrate with our existing order management system, Unicommerce, so that order status updates flow back there in real time.

stakeholders.name: Karan Malhotra
concerns: We need the system to auto-assign the nearest available rider to each order.
Proof of delivery is critical — every delivery needs a photo and either a signature or an OTP entered by the customer before it's marked complete.
We had a spike in "item not received" disputes last quarter and it cost us badly on chargebacks.
We also need this to integrate with our existing order management system, Unicommerce, so that order status updates flow back there in real time.
Last month we had a rider go completely off-route for two hours and nobody noticed until the customer called to complain, that shouldn't be able to happen again.
We need this live before the next big sale event, which is roughly ten weeks out.
The finance team has capped spend at 35 lakh for build plus first year of maps API costs.

stakeholders.name: Neha Iyer
concerns: The auto-assignment needs to consider both distance and current rider load — someone with three pending drops shouldn't get a fourth if there's a free rider two streets away.
Ideally the OTP should be sent to the customer automatically via SMS when the rider is within, say, 500 meters of the drop location.

stakeholders.name: Ravi Kumar
concerns: Riders need a mobile app that shows their route for the day, and it must work with patchy network — a lot of our delivery zones have poor connectivity. The app should queue updates offline and sync when signal comes back.

Failed deliveries need a reason code — customer not available, wrong address, refused — and those should automatically trigger a reattempt the next day, up to two attempts before we return it to the hub.
Riders are contract workers with their own phones, mostly older Android devices, so the app has to run acceptably on low-end Android, we can't assume everyone has a flagship phone.

stakeholders.name: Sameer Qureshi
concerns: For live tracking, the customer-facing tracking link needs to update the rider's location at least every 30 seconds.
Our maps and routing run on the Google Maps Platform, that's already contracted.
On scale, during the festive peak we hit 9,000 deliveries in a single day. The dispatch engine has to assign a rider within 10 seconds of an order coming in, even at that peak.

constraints: Our maps and routing run on the Google Maps Platform, that's already contracted.
The dispatch engine has to assign a rider within 10 seconds of an order coming in, even at peak (9,000 deliveries in a single day).
Riders are contract workers with their own phones, mostly older Android devices, so the app has to run acceptably on low-end Android.
We need this live before the next big sale event, which is roughly ten weeks out.
The finance team has capped spend at 35 lakh for build plus first year of maps API costs.
The rider mobile app must work with patchy network, queue updates offline and sync when signal comes back.
The customer-facing tracking link needs to update the rider's location at least every 30 seconds.
out_of_scope: Route optimization across an entire hub's deliveries — like solving the best order to visit 40 stops — is out of scope for this phase. We're doing single-order assignment only for now, batch routing is a phase two thing.
open_questions: What are the specific reason codes for failed deliveries beyond 'customer not available, wrong address, refused'?
What is the exact date of the 'next big sale event'?
What are the specific requirements for the 'photo' in proof of delivery (e.g., timestamp, geotagging, object detection)?
What are the specific requirements for 'signature' in proof of delivery (e.g., digital signature pad, finger signature on screen)?
What are the current metrics for manual dispatch time and accuracy?

epics.title: Efficient Order Dispatch
epics.goal: To ensure orders are automatically assigned to the most suitable rider quickly, optimizing delivery initiation.

epics.title: Seamless Delivery Execution
epics.goal: To provide riders with a reliable mobile application that supports efficient delivery completion, even in challenging network conditions.

epics.title: Robust Proof of Delivery
epics.goal: To implement comprehensive proof of delivery mechanisms that reduce disputes and ensure accountability for every delivery.

epics.title: Real-time Visibility & Control
epics.goal: To provide stakeholders with real-time tracking and alerts, enabling proactive management of deliveries and rider activities.

epics.title: Core Platform Integrations
epics.goal: To establish essential integrations with external systems for mapping, routing, and order management, ensuring smooth data flow.

stories.title: Auto-assign nearest available rider

stories.so_that: deliveries are initiated quickly and efficiently

acceptance_criteria.given: an unassigned order is received and multiple riders are available
acceptance_criteria.when: the auto-assignment engine runs
acceptance_criteria.then: the order is assigned to the rider with the shortest calculated distance to the pickup location

acceptance_criteria.then: the order is assigned to the available rider

acceptance_criteria.given: an unassigned order is received and two riders are equally near, but Rider A has 3 active deliveries and Rider B has 0 active deliveries
acceptance_criteria.when: the auto-assignment engine runs
acceptance_criteria.then: the order is assigned to Rider B

stories.title: Fast rider assignment

acceptance_criteria.given: an order is received and a suitable rider is available
acceptance_criteria.when: the system processes the order for assignment
acceptance_criteria.then: a rider is assigned within 10 seconds

acceptance_criteria.given: an order is received and a suitable rider is available, and the system is processing 100 other orders concurrently
acceptance_criteria.when: the system processes the order for assignment
acceptance_criteria.then: a rider is assigned within 10 seconds

issues: The "i_want" statement "manage my deliveries" implies significant functionality beyond just launching and logging in, which is not covered by the acceptance criteria.
The story combines the initial development of the mobile application (R-004) with a performance requirement (R-026) and a broad "core functionality" scope, making it too large and unfocused.
The acceptance criteria for "core functionality" are insufficient to define the full scope of "manage my deliveries" or "functional mobile application".
The term "remains responsive" in AC2 is subjective and not fully quantified, making it harder to test definitively.
reviews.fix_instructions: Split this story into at least two. One story should focus on the basic launch and login functionality (R-004) with specific ACs. Another story should address the performance on low-end Android devices (R-026) with more precise, measurable criteria for responsiveness. Ensure the "i_want" and ACs align for each new story.

gaps.description: The business goal of reducing "item not received" disputes and chargebacks is addressed by implementing proof of delivery, but there's no explicit requirement or story detailing how the captured proof of delivery data (photos, signatures, OTPs) will be stored, accessed, or utilized by relevant teams (e.g., customer service, finance) to actually resolve disputes or prevent chargebacks.
gaps.suggested_question: How will the captured proof of delivery data (photos, signatures, OTPs) be stored and made accessible to our customer service and finance teams to help resolve 'item not received' disputes and prevent chargebacks?

gaps.description: There are no explicit security requirements for the platform, rider mobile application, or the handling of sensitive data such as customer OTPs, location data, and personal order information. This is critical for a system handling personal and operational data.
gaps.suggested_question: What are our security requirements for data at rest and in transit, user authentication, and access control for the dispatch platform and rider app, especially concerning customer and rider personal data?

gaps.description: There are no requirements specifying data retention policies for critical information such as proof of delivery photos/signatures, rider location history, order dispatch logs, or failed delivery reasons. This is important for dispute resolution, compliance, and operational analysis.
gaps.suggested_question: What are the required data retention periods for proof of delivery records, rider location history, and other operational data, and how should this data be archived or purged?

gaps.description: There are no stated availability or uptime targets for the dispatch platform or the Unicommerce integration. As a critical operational system, understanding expected uptime and disaster recovery capabilities is essential.
gaps.suggested_question: What are the expected availability targets (e.g., uptime percentage) for the dispatch system and its integration with Unicommerce, and what are our disaster recovery expectations?

gaps.description: Requirement R-010 states a photo is required for proof of delivery, but lacks specific details on what constitutes an acceptable photo (e.g., timestamp, geotagging, content).
related_ids: Open Question: What are the specific requirements for the 'photo' in proof of delivery (e.g., timestamp, geotagging, object detection)?
gaps.suggested_question: For photo proof of delivery, do we need to capture timestamp, geotagging, or specific content (e.g., package clearly visible at door)? What are the minimum acceptable quality standards?

gaps.description: Requirement R-011 states a customer signature is required, but doesn't specify the method of capture (e.g., finger on screen, digital signature pad).
related_ids: Open Question: What are the specific requirements for 'signature' in proof of delivery (e.g., digital signature pad, finger signature on screen)?
gaps.suggested_question: For customer signatures, will riders capture these directly on their mobile device screens, or is there a different method expected?

gaps.description: Requirement R-028 states "relevant stakeholders" should be notified when a rider goes off-route, but does not specify who these stakeholders are or the preferred notification method.
gaps.suggested_question: Who are the specific stakeholders that need to be notified when a rider goes off-route, and what is the preferred method of notification for each (e.g., SMS, email, in-app alert)?

gaps.description: The customer service/support team is directly impacted by the system, particularly regarding "item not received" disputes, customer tracking inquiries, and failed delivery processes. They will need access to and tools for utilizing proof of delivery data.
gaps.suggested_question: Who from our customer service or support team should be involved to ensure the system meets their needs for handling customer inquiries and disputes related to deliveries?

gaps.description: The finance team is mentioned regarding budget constraints and chargebacks, but no specific finance stakeholder is listed. Their input is crucial for defining how PoD data supports chargeback prevention and for tracking project costs.
gaps.suggested_question: Who is the key contact from the finance team who can provide input on how proof of delivery data can best support chargeback prevention and manage project financials?

gaps.coverage_note: The backlog provides good coverage for the core functional requirements of rider dispatch, proof of delivery, and integration with Unicommerce and Google Maps. Key non-functional aspects like performance and offline capabilities for the rider app are also addressed. However, there are some critical areas that need further definition. The utility of proof of delivery data for dispute resolution is not fully specified, and important non-functional requirements like security, comprehensive data retention, and system availability targets are missing. Several requirements also need more specific details to avoid ambiguity in implementation. Finally, key operational stakeholders like customer service and a dedicated finance representative are not explicitly listed, whose input would be valuable for ensuring the system fully meets business needs.
